messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode of care described below. A three-character category is one capital letter followed by exactly two digits, for example J44.

Hospital course:
Hospital Course:
The patient, an 85-year-old male, was admitted to the hospital with bilateral foot swelling, decreased urine output, and a poor urinary stream. He also complained of breathlessness, anorexia, weight loss, and had a past medical history significant for anemia. Physical examination revealed multiple, nontender, firm lymph nodes in the right upper jugular, middle jugular, right and left submandibular, and multiple right-sided axillary lymph nodes. His laboratory investigations revealed findings consistent with tumor lysis syndrome, including elevated uric acid, hyperphosphatemia, and hypocalcemia. Bone marrow examination showed hypercellular smears with reduced megakaryocytes and erythropoiesis. The bone marrow differential counts revealed immature cells with monocytic differentiation and large collections of mature lymphocytes.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
Despite being explained about the treatment options and prognosis, the patient refused to undergo any further investigations and therapy.

Discharge Condition:
The patient was discharged home in fair condition. A follow-up plan was initiated with further medical management as an outpatient.

Reply with the three characters only.

text:
Likely diagnosis: chronic lymphocytic leukemia with acute myeloid/monocytic transformation, or acute monocytic leukemia plus CLL. The bone marrow shows immature cells with monocytic differentiation and a large collection of mature lymphocytes, which suggests acute monocytic leukemia coexisting with CLL. Tumor lysis syndrome is also present.

The principal diagnosis category is probably leukemia. For acute monocytic leukemia the code is C93 (monocytic leukemia), though C91 (CLL) is possible too. Because the lymphadenopathy and the mature lymphocytes point to CLL, while the immature monocytic cells point to acute disease, I'm going with the more active process, which is acute monocytic leukemia, C93. Tumor lysis syndrome is a complication that would be coded as E88.

C93
